findings.title: Profile-weight list comprehension violates the slice's "no per-agent Python loops" constraint
findings.description: The slice's defining technical constraint is "No Python-level per-agent loops in any `BulkForce.__call__` implementation" (Success Criteria, Technical Requirements), yet the documented vectorized pattern uses a Python list comprehension: `np.array([profiles[pi].cohesion_weight for pi in state.profile_indices[eval_indices]])`. The doc acknowledges this ("This is a Python list comprehension over `n` agents") but dismisses it as negligible at n=100. Two problems: (1) the verification grep in step 4 (`for.*agent_idx\|for.*eval_indices\|for.*list_idx`) won't catch this comprehension because it iterates over `state.profile_indices`, not `agent_idx`/`eval_indices` directly, so the "no per-agent Python loops remain" verification will pass even if the comprehension ships. (2) This is exactly the kind of Python-level per-agent dispatch that the architecture flags as a GPU-compat concern (100-arch.behavior-engine.md, "GPU compute path for force accumulation"). Either precompute a `(n_profiles, n_weight_fields)` weight table once at engine init and index into it with NumPy, or rename the constraint to acknowledge the per-tick profile-dispatch cost and document the GPU migration path. The constraint as written cannot be met by the documented pattern.

findings.title: No failure-mode enumeration for `build_neighbor_data()` I/O path
findings.description: The slice introduces a new per-tick I/O path (`build_neighbor_data()` consuming per-agent spatial query results) but does not enumerate its failure modes. Specifically: (a) what happens when `max_neighbors == 0` (all active agents have zero neighbors) — `NeighborData.indices` would have shape `(n_active, 0)`; (b) what happens when `active_indices` is empty (`n_active == 0`) — the cohesion example does `state.positions[neighbor_data.indices]` and `np.sum(neighbor_pos, axis=1)` which work on zero-sized arrays but produce empty outputs that must propagate correctly through downstream force accumulation and integration; (c) what happens if the spatial query returns more neighbors than expected (memory bound on `max_neighbors`) — should there be a truncation policy, an error, or unbounded growth. The "Handling Zero-Neighbor Agents" subsection covers per-row zero counts but not the case where the entire array's second dimension is 0. The doc should add an explicit failure-mode table for this new path.

findings.title: `WorldBoundsRepulsor` lives in a server-side slice, not the engine slice doc it cites
findings.description: The slice doc repeatedly cites `WorldBoundsRepulsor` as a "non-neighbor force" that already exists in the engine. In fact, slice 314 (`314-slice.repulsor-framework.md`) introduces `WorldBoundsRepulsor` as a new file in `migratory/engine/repulsor.py` and that slice is currently `not_started`. The 109 doc treats it as a pre-existing BulkForce that only needs its signature updated; in reality, depending on order, 109 may need to wait for 314 or update an interface that does not yet exist. Worth flagging for the implementation plan but not blocking the design.
